title: Fence the principle index against the skill dirs and the class vocabulary
action: Add packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/principle_index_parity.rs, modelled on packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/rule_index_parity.rs: pure filesystem, std only, nothing imported from the bee crate, and NO private copy of any list it guards. Pin four things. (1) Every skills/principle-*/ directory has exactly one row in the '## Principle homes' section, and every row names a directory that exists — both directions. (2) Every value on a row's `classes:` line appears in ROUTE_CLASS_VALUES, read as TEXT from packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/state_group/workflows.rs (the route_class_parity.rs technique). (3) Every row carries a non-empty `spoken:` line, and it sits BEFORE the row's `applied_at:` line. (4) Every row's guide anchor names a file under expertise/ that exists and a heading that appears in it.

truths: The fence declares no list of its own — class values are read from workflows.rs as text, principle names from the skills/ directory listing.
Dir-without-row and row-without-dir both go red.
A classes: value outside ROUTE_CLASS_VALUES goes red and names the offending value.

report.outcome: Added the principle-index parity fence: skills and rows both ways, classes read from ROUTE_CLASS_VALUES as text, spoken before applied_at, and guide anchors that resolve
report.tests: cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test principle_index_parity — green:unit — the cell own verify; the only test touched, and a mutation probe drove all four asserts red before the green
